corrections.proposed: 1935 (first pole tower); 1945 (present L-4 tower, a replacement)
corrections.why: The Register and firelookout.com both date the first 30-foot pole tower with open-air cab to about 1935; 1945 is the date given for the replacement tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 1945 and firelookout.com gives 1941 for the present tower. An April 1945 newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts describes a tower under construction that year, which supports 1945. The story reports both dates.
Three different names for the protective association appear across the Register, firelookout.com and the 1945 item. The story reports all three.
firelookout.com places the tower 16 miles southeast of Seeley Lake; the 1945 item places it seven miles southwest of Ovando. Those reference points do not agree, so the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: NHLR and firelookout.com agree on the first 30-foot pole tower (about 1935), the L-4 cab, the unused years and no public access. They disagree on the replacement year (1945 vs 1941), the builder's name, and the location reference. The record's 1945 built date is the replacement tower; a correction is proposed. The 1921 and 1945 items are quoted on the Forest Lookouts page only; they are not confirmed as the same site as the 1935 tower, though the 1945 item names Montour Mountain. The 1921 item does not name the mountain (July 3, 1921, The Missoulian), so the story says so. height_m 9.1 is 30 ft converted. Status kept standing: NHLR calls the tower abandoned, not removed. Access set to private from NHLR. Search results also showed Archives West and Montana Historical Society material on the Blackfoot Forest Protective Association, but only snippets were seen, so they are not cited. No photos added; firelookout.com credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum and Gary Weber with no image URLs.
